Attackers can supply a crafted input with a non-PCM multichannel audio stream remuxed to D-10 MXF to leak heap memory into the output file or crash the application.

Remote attackers can send 'TARGET COMMAND [ARG]' messages passed to avfilter_graph_send_command() to change filter runtime parameters and alter processed audio or video.

latest.description: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the deflicker filter that lets attackers corrupt heap memory via unclamped high bit depth luma samples. Attackers can supply crafted video whose luma values exceed the nominal depth, making calc_avgy16() increment counters past the histogram allocation, causing crashes or possibly code execution.

Attackers can supply crafted video with samples exceeding the nominal depth, passed unchanged by rawvideo, to crash the application or leak heap contents into output video.

latest.description: FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in recv_msg() of the zmq and azmq filters that allows unauthenticated network attackers to corrupt memory by sending oversized command messages. Attackers can send a 4 GiB message to the default listening port, truncating the int buffer size so memcpy() writes past the heap allocation and crashes FFmpeg.

latest.description: FFmpeg 4.3 before 9.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in the dynaudnorm filter because cqueue_resize() miscalculates gain history queue element counts when gausssize changes at runtime. Attackers can send gausssize commands via asendcmd scripts or an unauthenticated azmq filter to corrupt heap memory, crashing the process or potentially executing code.
